note: Attacker-controlled length byte of the ipAddress (0x87) GeneralName inside the subjectAltName extension; the PoC uses 6 (not 4 or 16).
GeneralName type is ipAddress, so the parser enters the ipAddress branch that is supposed to format the address into dNSName.

len is 6, not 4 (IPv4), so the snprintf() that fills dNSName is skipped; the else branch only contains a TODO comment and never writes dNSName. The 256-byte stack buffer stays uninitialized and is not NUL-terminated.
First string-processing routine applied to the never-initialized dNSName buffer: it lowercases len bytes read from uninitialized stack memory, propagating the uninitialized value.
ndpi_is_printable_string() branches on the uninitialized dNSName bytes, consuming the tainted value.
server_names is NULL on this fresh flow, so ndpi_strdup(dNSName) is called; ndpi_strdup internally runs strlen() over the uninitialized buffer.
strlen() scans the uninitialized dNSName buffer for a NUL terminator that was never written, reading uninitialized stack memory (use-of-uninitialized-value under MemorySanitizer).
